name: Paraneoplastic Uveitis

criteria.description: Presence of intraocular inflammation consistent with uveitis confirmed by ophthalmologic examination
Identification of an underlying malignancy temporally associated with uveitis
Exclusion of infectious, autoimmune, and other known causes of uveitis
Detection of paraneoplastic autoantibodies associated with ocular inflammation (e.g., anti-recoverin antibodies)
Improvement of uveitis with treatment of underlying malignancy and/or immunosuppressive therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of intraocular inflammation consistent with uveitis, confirmed underlying malignancy, and exclusion of other causes of uveitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by exclusion of other etiologies and presence of malignancy; paraneoplastic antibodies may aid but are not always present.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic bilateral inflammation of the anterior uveal tract
searchTerms: eye redness and pain in both eyes
granuloma in front part of both eyes

pathognomonic.notes: Inflammation of retinal vessels often seen in paraneoplastic uveitis

common.notes: Visual disturbances caused by inflammatory debris in vitreous humor
searchTerms: spots or floaters in vision from eye inflammation
seeing floaters due to vitreous issues
visual floaters caused by eye inflammation

common.notes: Light sensitivity secondary to uveal inflammation
Blurred vision due to intraocular inflammation
Involvement of choroid and retina in inflammatory process

occasional.notes: Swelling of optic nerve head due to inflammation
Fluid accumulation in macula causing central vision impairment
Layering of inflammatory cells in anterior chamber
searchTerms: pus layer in front eye chamber
white blood cell accumulation in eye
fluid buildup in anterior eye chamber

occasional.notes: Pain around the eye related to inflammation

rare.notes: Elevated intraocular pressure due to inflammatory blockage
Separation of retina due to severe inflammation
Abnormal blood vessel growth in choroid secondary to inflammation

laboratory: Presence of paraneoplastic autoantibodies (e.g., anti-recoverin, anti-enolase)
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) may be present
imaging: Fluorescein angiography showing retinal vasculitis and leakage
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating macular edema and retinal thickening
Ultrasound B-scan may reveal vitreous opacities
other: Identification of underlying malignancy via imaging (CT, PET scan)
Histopathological confirmation of tumor if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Association with systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., sarcoidosis, Behçet's disease)
Neoplastic infiltration of the eye (e.g., lymphoma)
Atypical clinical course and poor response to immunosuppression
Diagnostic ocular biopsy may be required

redFlags: Presence of systemic malignancy symptoms (weight loss, night sweats)
Poor response to standard uveitis therapies
references: Chan CC, et al. Paraneoplastic Autoimmune Retinopathy and Uveitis. Surv Ophthalmol. 2019;64(4):456-466.
Ding X, et al. Paraneoplastic Uveitis: Clinical Features and Management. Ocul Immunol Inflamm. 2021;29(5):789-796.
